sections.heading: Jake White emerges as the leading candidate to coach the Flying Fijians
sections.body: The Flying Fijians have reportedly identified former South Africa boss Jake White as the leading contender to become their new head coach ahead of the 2027 Rugby World Cup. The World Cup-winning coach joins a high-profile shortlist to succeed Mick Byrne, who parted ways with Fiji Rugby by mutual agreement in April. With 31 applicants vying for the vacancy, White's candidacy intensifies the search as the national side prepares for the upcoming northern hemisphere tour, which begins next month against France.

lead.why: Jake White has emerged as the leading candidate to become the next Fiji head coach, representing a major development in the ongoing coaching search.

sections.heading: England trail South Africa and New Zealand in Nations Championship ticket sales
sections.body: Tickets for South Africa and New Zealand's Nations Championship finals-weekend visits to Twickenham have sold out, but those to watch England in their own tournament finale remain on general sale at £164.80, the Guardian reports. Organisers say 60-65% of all finals-weekend tickets have sold, with England's last Twickenham outing — a 42-21 defeat by Ireland in their worst Six Nations campaign — doing little to stir home demand ahead of pool fixtures against Australia, Japan and New Zealand next month.

sections.body: French second-tier club Provence Rugby hosted NBA superstar Victor Wembanyama for a fortnight of physical and mental preparation during his summer off-season. sections.heading: Ireland women secure consecutive victories with a seven-try win over Japan
sections.body: The Ireland women's squad secured consecutive victories over Japan with a comprehensive 43-19 win at Virgin Media Park on Saturday. Scott Bemand's side scored seven tries, recovering from an early deficit to lead 22-7 at half-time. Brittany Hogan and Beibhinn Parsons both crossed the line, with Parsons extending her record to 25 international tries, while debutants Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett scored after coming off the bench. The squad now travels to South Africa for their WXV campaign with significant momentum.

lead.why: Ireland women's comprehensive seven-try victory over Japan completes consecutive wins before their WXV campaign.

sections.heading: Steve Lancaster Rules Out Australian Leg Of 2029 Lions Tour
sections.body: New Zealand Rugby chief executive Steve Lancaster has ruled out staging any of the 2029 British & Irish Lions fixtures in Australia, despite reports the Melbourne Cricket Ground was in the frame as a bigger venue option. Lancaster said a Test across the Tasman was 'not acceptable' to NZ Rugby, with every game now set for Aotearoa. It is a tour many expect to lean heavily on Ireland's current crop, with a fourth Test discussed but ultimately shelved.

lead.why: The only live men's international story in today's pack, and it touches the Lions tour that will define several Ireland careers.

sections.heading: Italy sit eleventh in the table following three consecutive tournament defeats
sections.body: Italy sit eleventh in the Nations Championship standings after suffering three straight losses in their opening tournament fixtures. Gonzalo Quesada's men have struggled to find their rhythm, scoring 37 points across those three matches. Defensively, they have conceded 131 points in that same three-game span, a run that culminated in a 10-57 defeat against Australia in their last outing. Historically, the side reached their highest ever world ranking of No. 8 in both 2007 and 2024.

lead.why: There is no active news coverage of the team today, so this edition focuses on the tournament standings and historical rankings.

sections.heading: The Welsh Rugby Union slashes ticket prices to £10 for Australia

Sluggish sales are also affecting Wales' other home fixtures, with around 36,000 tickets still available for the meeting with Japan and 30,000 left for the New Zealand match.

sections.heading: Argentina puts forward eight stadiums in joint 2035 World Cup bid
sections.body: The Argentine Rugby Union has submitted its technical proposal to World Rugby, nominating eight domestic stadiums for the joint 2035 Rugby World Cup bid. Argentina is leading the four-nation project alongside Uruguay, Chile and Brazil, with famous venues like Buenos Aires' Estadio Monumental and Rio de Janeiro's Maracanã included. Union president Félix Páez Molina hailed the bid as a vital step, as the South American coalition prepares to compete against Japan and Spain before the hosting decision in November 2027.

lead.why: It introduces official comments from union president Félix Páez Molina and highlights the specific stadium submissions for the 2035 World Cup bid.

sections.heading: Tom Hooper returns to Exeter Chiefs after early release from Wallabies squad
sections.body: Exeter Chiefs director of rugby Rob Baxter has confirmed Wallabies forward Tom Hooper has returned to England and could feature in Sunday's Premiership match against Newcastle. The 25-year-old was released from the Australia squad ahead of the Bledisloe Cup series because the Tests fall outside World Rugby's regulation nine window. Hooper, who made 23 appearances for Exeter last season, has had a 10-day break and is eager to play, with Baxter noting that if they select him, "it'll be a bench situation."

sections.body: Hunter Paisami's suspension for his tackle on Sacha Feinberg-Mngomezulu was cut only from six matches to four on appeal, still ruling the first-choice inside centre out of Saturday's Bledisloe opener at Eden Park and the Sydney rematch. Justin Marshall called the sanction "an absolute joke," with Jeremy Paul and Kieran Read agreeing it was harsh given Feinberg-Mngomezulu played on unaffected. The blow deepens Les Kiss's midfield concerns, with Paisami's partner Len Ikitau still nursing a bone-bruised ankle from the Springboks win in Perth.

sections.heading: Kieran Read urges Dave Rennie to centre back-row on Peter Lakai
sections.body: Former captain Kieran Read has urged Dave Rennie to prioritise Peter Lakai as the cornerstone of the All Blacks’ back-row for the upcoming Bledisloe Cup series. With Ardie Savea and Luke Jacobson sidelined by injury, Read argued that New Zealand needs to resolve the uncertainty in their loose forward combinations to match the stability of the Wallabies. He noted that while the squad possesses significant individual talent, they have yet to find the cohesive rhythm required to dominate the breakdown.

lead.why: It addresses a central tactical question concerning the All Blacks' forward balance ahead of the Bledisloe Cup.

sections.heading: Steve Lancaster confirms All Blacks will not play Lions in Australia
sections.body: New Zealand Rugby CEO Steve Lancaster has clarified that all matches for the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour will take place within Aotearoa. Responding to reports that a Test could be moved to the Melbourne Cricket Ground to maximise revenue, Lancaster stated such a move was not acceptable. While he acknowledged the challenge of balancing limited local stadium capacities with the financial demands of the modern game, he maintained that the team would not prioritise offshore fixtures at the expense of home fans.

lead.why: The CEO's comments provide a significant, new policy update regarding the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour.

sections.heading: Steve Lancaster rules out Australia hosting 2029 Lions Test match
sections.body: New Zealand Rugby chief executive Steve Lancaster has confirmed the 2029 British and Irish Lions tour will be played entirely in Aotearoa, ruling out suggestions a Test could be staged in Australia. Lancaster revealed the tourists have raised concerns about revenue given New Zealand's smaller stadiums, but insisted, "I don't think people should worry that we're going to turn the All Blacks into the Harlem Globetrotters." He confirmed all matches, including any fourth Test under discussion, will stay on home soil.

lead.why: A fresh, newly-reported story straight from NZ Rugby's CEO on Lions scheduling, not a rehash of the back-row theme already covered this week.

sections.heading: World Rugby bans 'hip drop' tackle following Springboks' injury concerns
sections.body: World Rugby has officially outlawed the 'hip drop' and 'knee drop' tackles, effective from 1 November. The decision follows a review by an expert tackle height working group, with the former move specifically targeted after Springboks coach Felix Jones campaigned against the technique. The move comes as a direct response to the impact of such tackles on player welfare, exemplified by the incident that previously sidelined South Africa forward Elrigh Louw for 10 months with severe leg injuries.

lead.why: It reports a significant regulatory change directly influenced by Springbok coaching staff to improve player welfare.

sections.heading: World Rugby outlaws hip-drop tackle following Felix Jones' request over Louw
sections.body: Felix Jones' push to protect his players has paid off, with World Rugby outlawing the hip-drop and knee-drop tackles that nearly ended Elrigh Louw's career in early 2025. The Springboks loose forward spent ten months out with knee ligament damage and a broken leg from the tackle, and the new law — carrying a penalty sanction — comes into force this November, ahead of the Boks' Round 4 trip to face Italy.

lead.why: A genuine rule change driven by a Springboks coach after a Bok was nearly ended by injury beats routine club team-news or NZ chatter.
